text:
monica.docs: holding PR #4251 until we confirm default content-filtering and streaming concurrency behavior. preview showed an example that might imply filtering is automatic for hosted but not for Dedicated. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4251
ci-bot: docs-preview: snapshot mismatch on /api-reference/generate (build 820) :warning:
arjun.runtime: can you paste the example you used? is this about `content_filter` vs `content_filtering`?
monica.docs: example from the guide:
```json
POST /v1/generate
{ "model":"redwood-qa","input":"what's X?","stream":true }
```
preview text said: "Hosted routes automatically apply content_filtering; Dedicated customers must opt in." that's a strong claim, want to make sure it's correct.
lucy.sdk: SDK note: we expose `content_filtering` boolean in the client options (JS/Python). default used to be `true` in early hosted-only docs but was later changed to `false` to avoid breaking behaviors. current released SDK default is `false`.
arjun.runtime: authoritative platform behavior: content filtering is a policy that can be applied at three layers: (1) organization/global policy (applies to hosted by default in new orgs), (2) route-level config `route.content_filtering` (defaults to false unless organization policy enforces it), (3) SDK client-level `content_filtering` (client opt-in/out). So the docs should avoid saying "hosted automatically filters" unless you mean "new hosted orgs may have org policy enabled".
sam.sec: security addendum: for regulated customers we enforce org-level `content_filtering=true` by contract. call that out in the enterprise section rather than general API reference.
emma.qe: small but important: streaming + filtering interaction: if filtering blocks content mid-stream we send an error event over SSE and close the stream (no silent truncation). please document that behavior. QE has a test case.
lucy.sdk: also nuance: SDK v2 (beta) will change default to `true` for hosted-first flows; release timeline Q2. we need a migration note.
monica.docs: ok to summarize: (1) org policy can enforce filtering for hosted customers (callout in enterprise section), (2) route-level default is false, (3) SDK default is false in released 1.x, v2 flips to true. and (4) streaming + filter=when-blocked -> send SSE `event: error` then close. can you confirm wording?
arjun.runtime: correct. precise phrasing suggestion: "Content filtering is controlled by org, route, and client settings. Without an explicit org or route policy, the server does not automatically filter; clients can opt in. For orgs with enforced policies (typical in enterprise contracts), filtering applies to all routes."
lucy.sdk: i'll add the SDK snippet for the migration guide: ```js
// opt into filtering on SDK 1.x
const client = new Redwood({ key: KEY, content_filtering: true });
await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-qa', input, stream: true });
```
ci-bot: docs-preview: rebuild requested for PR 4251 (build 821)
devops-bot: triggered preview build 821. logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/821 :robot_face:
ci-bot: docs-preview: success (build 821) :tada:
emma.qe: tested SSE behavior: when filter triggers mid-stream we publish SSE with `event: filter_block` then `event: error` with code `CONTENT_FILTER` in the final payload. please include that exact event name and code in the reference.
arjun.runtime: confirmation: event name `filter_block` then `final_error` payload with code `CONTENT_FILTER` is our current contract. i'll file a tiny runtime note in the API reference so it's explicit.
monica.docs: great. i'll update PR text with the org vs route vs SDK table, add the SSE event names and the SDK migration snippet. assigning reviewers: @lucy.sdk, @arjun.runtime. holding merge until one approval.
lucy.sdk: LGTM from SDK docs side. minor nit on wording. approved.
arjun.runtime: approving. merge when green.
monica.docs: merging after squash. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
